composition: Add these distinct mandatory rows to the parent denominator; no existing obligation or failure is removed.

rows.observableExpectedBehavior: An explicit retry or correction exposes its actual next required action, including an earlier screen position. Deferred focus retains the explicit operation reason after controls unlock. Ordinary forward progress retains its prohibition against upward auto-scroll.
rows.requiredEvidence: Execute the original complete operator path: Save, export, ingest a wrong-project response, reject it, activate replacement attempt, and inspect next-action visibility without driver scrolling. Add independent controlled-geometry failures for the explicit retry caller and deferred reason preservation, then replay the real browser journey and affected correction paths.
rows.applicableStages: Every stage permitting retry or correction, derived from the workflow
rows.actual: The complete actual-controls journey failed at Stage 1 before operator action 2 because #next-required-action remained above the viewport after #prepare-replacement-attempt. The production caller used the forward default despite an explicit retry; the shared pending-focus owner also retained the node but not its reason.

rows.observableExpectedBehavior: Creating a disposable project does not rewrite unrelated existing projects or defeat their History compare-and-swap protections. Independent project creation and bulk-transaction fault verification remain separate operations.
rows.requiredEvidence: Replay the existing failed browser sequence using create-only persistence for the new fixture, and verify that existing projects retain their exact state; retain the deliberate bulk-transaction concurrency negative case separately.
rows.applicableStages: Project creation at any selected stage
rows.actual: verify-browser.mjs:129 called writeAll with previously read copies of every project while a view checkpoint could advance History. Production correctly rejected the stale history generation with Project History changed in another tab.

rows.sourceLocation: operator section 6.C complete retained History and exact file bytes; sections 8 and 10
rows.observableExpectedBehavior: Backup evidence accounts for active stored files, every promised checkpoint and retained file bytes. Derive expected membership from recorded project and recovery identities, reject missing, unexpected or duplicate members, verify each member's bytes, then restore and compare the corresponding complete recovery state.
rows.requiredEvidence: Actual paged artifact download and full exported backup under bounded-read instrumentation; compare the exact independently recorded expected member set, per-member byte sizes/hashes and restored history rather than assuming active canonical file count equals complete archive count.
rows.applicableStages: All stages with active or retained files
rows.actual: The test expected 22 archive members although the exported backup contained 49 members including retained History. The selected final file, its tail, package hash and restored canonical artifact count had already matched. This is not evidence that History members may be dropped.

rows.sourceLocation: operator section 6.B validation versus acceptance; sections 7-8 and 10
rows.observableExpectedBehavior: An otherwise valid response missing required returned bytes, or awaiting corrected mismatching bytes, keeps its recoverable reservation in RESPONSE_STAGED. The verifier reads canonical nested fields through the shared record accessors and reports the complete validation issues; genuinely nonrecoverable violations remain rejected.
rows.requiredEvidence: Execute missing-file rejection, mismatching-file rejection and corrected-file successful progression through actual controls, retaining raw validation and reservation observations and exact returned-byte comparison.
rows.applicableStages: Every stage with required returned attachments
rows.actual: verify-browser-extra.mjs:157 failed its reservation-state assertion after displaying MISSING_REQUIRED_ATTACHMENT. Its lookup read top-level record fields rather than the canonical accessor. Whether the reservation itself was incorrectly rejected must be established from the actual full record and validation output, not inferred from this assertion.
